--- title: "Counting backwards (11–20)" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · MATE_CONTAR_H_ATRAS_2A_DECENA" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (A · Accuracy; quality class A). Generated on November 27, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea MATE_CONTAR_H_ATRAS_2A_DECENA`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Contar hacia atrás (2.ª decena)*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/MATE_CONTAR_H_ATRAS_2A_DECENA.html). ::: **In one sentence.** Counting backwards (11–20), at age 5 (1,226 administrations in 2 cohorts). AUC .63 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 2032 | | Battery | LEEDUCA | | Format | rapid naming of a series | | Items | 2 (2032) according to the platform | | Task family | A · Accuracy | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | The child starts counting backwards from a given number. The counting stops after 5 numbers or when the child fails. | ## How it is programmed on the platform The platform is the reference: what the activity actually presents is what is measured. Configuration read from the activity itself on 23/10/2026 (without modifying it). Cell contents are in Spanish. | Code|Name on the platform |Presentation | Test items| Practice items|Example items |Time limit |Order |Scoring | Age.term (label 3)| |----:|:--------------------------------|:-------------------------|----------:|--------------:|:-------------|:----------|:-----|:--------|------------------:| | 2032|Contar - Hacia Atrás - 2ª Decena |Evaluador marca cada paso | 2| 0|— |— |fijo |Aciertos | 5| **Differences from the dictionary or the instructions (in Spanish):** - **2032.** Dos series hacia atrás (desde 16 y 13). *Age.term: provisional reading of the activity's label 3 (3rd digit = age, 4th = term; 0 = annual), to be confirmed with the engineer.* **How it looks on the platform** (first item or example; 2026 screenshot; the interface is in Spanish). ::: {layout-ncol=1} ![2032 · Contar - Hacia Atrás - 2ª Decena](../../figuras/plataforma/2032.jpg){.lightbox width="40%" fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 2032"} ::: ## Theoretical framework Counting forwards and backwards, and reading Arabic numerals, measure **symbolic number knowledge**: the verbal sequence of numerals and its correspondence with digits. This is learned knowledge, distinct from the approximate number sense (comparing quantities), and it forms the basis of school arithmetic. **What the evidence says:** - **Counting in preschool predicts mathematics in the first school years.** Mastery of counting principles at age 5 predicts the risk of mathematical difficulties in Grade 1 [@stock2009markers]. In Spanish children, the verbal number sequence (procedural counting) was the preschool task with the most weight in Grade 2 mathematics achievement [@mercader2017basicas]. - **Knowing Arabic numerals is one of the two pillars of early arithmetic.** In 569 children, only number knowledge and quantity discrimination uniquely predicted arithmetic progress in the first school year [@malone2020number]. Children with mathematical difficulties already show symbolic deficits in preschool, and those deficits persist [@desoete2012comparison]. - **Counting backwards is more demanding** than counting forwards. It requires retrieving the sequence in reverse order and holding it in working memory, which is why it discriminates better at age 5. **What our data show.** The four tasks have high internal consistency (α = .84–.95), but they were given in one or two sessions and there is no stability between terms. They predict later reading fluency poorly (AUC .53–.59), which supports their discriminant validity. Against low arithmetic at ages 10–11, counting backwards in the second ten is the most specific: AUC .67 vs. .51 for reading ([Numerical cognition](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/cognicion-numerica.html#sec-mate-criterio), *in Spanish*). ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 5.3| 2011| 159|2016/17 | 884| 0| 884| 34| | 5.3| 2012| 192|2017/18 | 342| 338| 0| 16| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----------:|---:|-------:|----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 5.3| 338| 2012| 2.20| 2.39| 1| 0.64| 36.09| 20.71| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning; the possible range is 0–6 correct responses. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. |Possible range | Warning| |----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|:--------------|-------:| | 5.3| 338|0–6 |0–6 |0–6 | | ## Reliability There are no two time points with the same children (at least 80). α (2021) = .93. ## Validity **Concurrent.** Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Phonological awareness (5.3, r = .46). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .63. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .60. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_MATE_CONTAR_H_ATRAS_2A_DECENA_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .56 (1 time point; 327–327 children). Against low arithmetic at ages 10–11 ([provisional criterion](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/cognicion-numerica.html#sec-mate-criterio), *in Spanish*), AUC .67. ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|-------:|--:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 5.3| 338| 2012| 0| 0| 0| 0| 1| 5| 6| **Floor effect.** At 5.3 P10 coincides with the worst possible score (at 5.3, P25 too): many children are tied at the minimum and the norms do not distinguish between them. At those time points this task cannot be used to grade difficulty. These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_MATE_CONTAR_H_ATRAS_2A_DECENA_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|-----:|------:|--:| |School SES (ρ) | 5.3| 1,200| 0.138| 0| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 5.3| 1,221| -0.298| 0| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 5.3| 1,212| 0.197| 0| |School (ICC) | 5.3| 1,226| 0.066| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Counting backwards (11–20)” (code 2032; LEEDUCA battery) assesses verbal number sequence. The child names a series of familiar stimuli on the screen as quickly as possible, and the examiner records correct responses and errors. It comprises 6 items. The time limit is 30 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2011 and 2012 cohorts it was administered in 2 sessions, from 5 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .93 (N = 1,227, 6 items). Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .60. ## Pending issues - Ceiling effect at 5.3 (more than 15% of children with the maximum score). - Floor effect at 5.3 (more than 15% with zero correct). - Floor effect in the norms at 5.3: at least 10% of children have the worst possible score, so P10 does not exist. At those time points the "severe" and "very severe" levels must not be assigned with this task (study M3). - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
